title: Holistic interdisciplinary medical diabetes group training for children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes in a child-friendly, real-life setting
summary:
Type 1 diabetes is one of the most common chronic diseases in children and adolescents. Age-appropriate care is essential in order to meet the individual needs and requirements of young people.

Those involved in the GaDiaKi project will develop and test new, age-appropriate, and holistic diabetes training programs for children and adolescents. The new form of care aims to improve self-management, i.e., the independent handling of their disease by children and adolescents and their independence. Innovative aspects of the program include the everyday setting of the training (e.g., leisure facilities) and the involvement of young adults with type 1 diabetes, who provide support to both the team and the children and adolescents. The researchers expect this to improve therapy satisfaction, independence, and quality of life for children and adolescents with diabetes.

To test the effectiveness of the concept, children and adolescents across Germany are being trained in groups of 15 to 20 for five to seven days by an interprofessional team comprising specialists in pediatric and adolescent diabetology, psychology, social pedagogy, and nutritional counseling, among others. The same number of children and adolescents will receive standard treatment. Every six months, the groups will be compared with each other, for example in terms of therapy satisfaction.

The project will be funded for three years with a total of approximately 4.4 million euros.

If successful, the results will contribute to improving the care of children and adolescents with diabetes through age-appropriate care and diabetes self-management.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children and adolescents with type 1 diabetes, duration of diabetes > 6 months ,
- Pediatric and adolescent diabetes centers participating in the Diabetes Patient Follow-up Documentation (DPV) program.
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of evaluation data at inclusion (Baseline)
- Lack of group capability and trainability of the children and adolescents
